correctness.rationale: A complete polarity-image classification follows by splitting input edge families into pairwise-intersecting families (star or triangle) and those containing disjoint edges (every polar contained in a four-cycle). Every four-cycle subset is realized by adding opposite cross-edges as blockers. All listed families are counted disjointly. Third-edge closedness counts 2n-5 versus 4 recover adjacency for n>=5, giving the sharp automorphism jump. A five-vertex closed-set triple violates the modular law. Direct independent finite checker covers all 33,864 input subsets through n=6 and shapes through n=9; no finite search is substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The exact lattice of overlapping edges on K_n is a canonical FCA structure with combinatorial and logical motivation. The all-n closed-set classification yields quartic vs exponentially many possible attribute sets; the automorphism jump at n=4 and exact modularity threshold are nontrivial structural invariants, not small numerical improvements. The result separates overlap from disjointness and identifies precisely what extra structure overlap recovers.
